candidate.call_site_files: 152 files carry the B34 allocator-call SAFETY blocks; 155 files are changed in total

stop_status: NO_STOP_DEFECT. NEO-ERR-6 (safe-interface soundness) and NEO-ERR-7 (allocator-hook reentrancy) are repaired in code; NEO-ERR-3/4 are contract-only for provenance/extent with one cheap authority-compatible check added. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE; the full ERR mechanism remains CONTRACTED and the consumer scope remains ESTABLISHED.

authority.abi: C ABI unchanged. The four entry points keep the exported names CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_zalloc/CRYPTO_calloc/CRYPTO_malloc_array, the same parameters, return types and extern "C" calling convention; only their Rust-callability changed (safe -> unsafe). No #[repr(C)] layout, allocator-seam size/file/line coordinate, or exported symbol changed.
external_contracts: CRYPTO_malloc/zalloc/calloc/malloc_array `file` is NULL or a NUL-terminated C string valid for the call; the allocation-failure/overflow path and the installed allocator hook may read it.

CRYPTO_realloc/clear_realloc/realloc_array/clear_realloc_array/free/clear_free/memdup/strdup/strndup/aligned_alloc/_array carry the same `file` clause in addition to their existing pointer/extent contracts.

OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/save_to_mark clear (and therefore release) the destination; every MALLOCED slot in the destination must be an exclusively owned seam block from a state produced by OSSL_ERR_STATE_new (or satisfy the slot contract).

OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore trusts err_data_size as the source extent, requires err_file/err_func to be NULL or NUL-terminated until return, requires no concurrent mutation, and now treats an out-of-range top/bottom as an empty state.

A hook installed by CRYPTO_set_mem_functions may re-enter ERR on the same thread; the nested access is refused (None) instead of aliasing the outer &mut. The external installer contract from B33 is retained as defence in depth.

boundaries.operation: CRYPTO_malloc-family `file` argument on the safe-interface boundary
boundaries.before: CRYPTO_malloc, CRYPTO_zalloc, CRYPTO_calloc and CRYPTO_malloc_array were safe extern "C" fns. A safe Rust caller could pass an arbitrary *const c_char; the failure/overflow path read it via c_strlen -> UB.
boundaries.after: All four are `pub unsafe extern "C" fn` with a # Safety contract requiring NULL or a NUL-terminated string valid for the call. The internal helpers malloc_request/alloc/dealloc/clear_dealloc/report_alloc_err/raise_integer_overflow are unsafe fns with the same clause. Every other allocator entry point's existing # Safety gained the `file` clause. 247 in-crate call sites across 152 files now carry a SAFETY-commented block. Each passes NULL, a static coordinate (C literal, module constant, or type-associated constant), or an enclosing helper parameter; 24 forward a private helper parameter and are recorded in R-ERR-10.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED for safe Rust callers: the unsafe read is no longer reachable through a safe fn. The precondition is now a caller obligation at every call site, and the C ABI remains byte-identical.

boundaries.before: with_state held &mut ErrState across allocation/release. An installed allocator hook that re-entered ERR on the same thread formed a second &mut: UB. The rule lived only in prose/external contract.
boundaries.after: A thread-local Cell<bool> (STATE_IN_USE) is acquired before the state is touched (and before load_crypto_strings). A nested with_state returns None without touching the state; the nested raise is dropped and the outer call completes. StateAccessGuard's Drop resets the flag on every exit path, including an unwinding closure. The module note and with_state docs were updated; the B33 external contract at CRYPTO_set_mem_functions is retained.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED (second &mut is inexpressible; the reentrant call fails closed with the existing no-state outcome).

boundaries.before: B33 documented the destination contract but left it as prose only.
boundaries.after: The # Safety blocks keep the full destination provenance/exclusive-ownership/no-concurrent-mutation contract. No runtime validation was added: no provenance marker exists in the public #[repr(C)] ERR_STATE layout, and adding one would change the ABI. Kept contract-only and recorded as retained.
boundaries.mechanism: RELOCATED to an external contract (no ABI-compatible runtime check).

boundaries.before: B33 stated the per-slot extent, NUL-termination and no-concurrent-mutation contract but trusted top/bottom unconditionally.
boundaries.after: The contract is retained and one cheap authority-compatible validation was added: top/bottom outside 0..ERR_STATE_SLOTS is treated as an empty state, so a hostile C state cannot index out of bounds or make the ring walk non-terminating. err_data_size remains trusted as the extent (a bounded copy would change authority behaviour and no provenance metadata exists).

unsafe_accounting.boundary_size_delta: The allocator seam's Rust surface is now 4 unsafe entry points plus 7 unsafe internal helpers; every in-crate caller establishes NULL-or-NUL-termination in a SAFETY-commented block. with_state gains one thread-local guard (no new unsafe op; the existing &mut formation is now reached at most once per thread). restore gains one bounds check. No unsafe operation was removed: the unsafe read still exists at the C boundary and in the allocator hook, but it is no longer reachable from safe Rust.
